placement.position_note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-3605). siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5.5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn on this record's stable key from the stocks its household class may hang (5 in, 5.5 in or 6 in; T-1839, docs/LIBERTIES.md L352), then advanced within them so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

occupants.value: S. Abell, attorney and counsellor — attorney, counsellor and land conveyancer
occupants.note: SEATED BY THE STREET-FACE ADOPTION POLICY (docs/STREET-FACE-ADOPTION.md, the owner's ruling of 2026-08-29 for T-0354, extended 2026-08-30 for T-0416; liberty L212). The newspaper register places this business on Dearborn Street AND NOTHING NARROWER — 2 printings, 1835-06-24 to 1835-08-01, claims chicago_american_1835_08_01#c003, chicago_democrat_1835_06_24#c006 — so it takes the STREET FACE and not a lot. THE ROOF ENDS ITS PLATTED TIER AGAINST Dearborn Street, so it is a corner building and stands on that street as well as on the one its lot faces — the owner's ruling of 2026-08-30 (T-0416). Nothing about the roof changed and no geometry was raised to seat this business. WHICH roof on that face it is given is an allocation by tools/adopt_street_faces.py and not a reading of any source, and nothing here says this business stood nearer the corner than any other on the same face. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption: the business is documented, the building under it is not, and this attribute is graded `reconstructed` because the invented part is the whole of the placement.

Neither roof is recorded for this person in 1835 (L354); the keeper is not invented.

persons.name: Sidney Abell
persons.note: A CONTEMPORARY CHICAGO PAPER OF 1833-1835 PRINTS THIS PERSON BY NAME IN THE TOWN. Read from directory_1843, newspaper_1833_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1b), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. newspaper_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 1 August 1835 and nothing says when they came. THE BOUND FALLS AFTER THE SCENE DATE and the record says so rather than narrowing it: the earliest source that names this person is later than 1 July 1835, so they may have arrived after the day this scene models. present_on_scene_date is `uncertain` for that reason. No figure is drawn (L1). THE SECOND PRESBYTERIAN ROLL — A NAME ON A CHURCH LIST THAT OPENS IN 1842, AND NEVER AN 1835 FACT. The 1892 printed membership roll of the Second Presbyterian Church of Chicago, read line by line into this repository, carries 1 line whose surname and given initial agree with this person's — “Abell, Sidney | Profession. | May 4, 1844. | Dismissed,” (second_presb_0385, printed page 176), admitted 1844-05-04 by profession. Under the rule that decided it: Surname 'Abell' folds to the same string as the roll line's, and the given name of both begins S. WHAT THE MATCH MINTS OR REGRADES: “NOTHING. A line on a roll that opens in June 1842 cannot place a person in the town of July 1835, and this file makes no proposal that it does. What a match IS: the same surname and initial, in Chicago, within seven years — a lead for a later pass that is allowed to write people.” This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE: under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the roll is handed to the card as a thing a reader may weigh, and the verdict stays with T-0515, which applies the ladder against every source at once.

residents.research_note: MINTED FROM THE CONSOLIDATED CIVIC, CHURCH, PRESS, BOOK AND CENSUS EVIDENCE (T-0513, T-0514). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here is written unattested in its own block, because the lists that name this person name a person and not a family. What is claimed is that the sources cited on the member below name them at Chicago, and the grade is the owner's ratified ladder applied by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py --build and spent by tools/mint_civic_residents.py, which prints every refusal. docs/LIBERTIES.md L215 carries the liberty and the tension with L213.

anything at all from an engraving — the cuts are the printer's stock

citations.citation: The Chicago Democrat. Vol. I, No. 1 (November 26, 1833) through Vol. II, No. 18 (August 26, 1835). Chicago, Ill.: John Calhoun, editor and publisher. Seventy-three issues, OCR-assisted research transcriptions from page scans.
what_it_supplies: that a named trade was being carried on in Chicago in a named week, and often where
self-reported addresses, which are the strongest address evidence this project has: the advertiser was paying, and his customers had to find him
dissolution, removal and replacement notices — the only thing that keeps a documented business out of the 1835 town under the owner's ruling 3
post-office letter lists, naming residents by the hundred (ruling 1: a listed name mints a resident candidate, flagged letter_list_only)
the village and later town ordinances, printed complete — the 7 November 1833 code is the richest single item in the run
arrivals and clearances, which date the piers and the harbour as working structures
public notices that fix a building as a polling place, an auction site or a meeting place on a given day
the paper's own imprint, self-reported: the corner of South Water and Clark streets
twenty-one months of continuous weekly attestation ending three weeks before the scene date, including the issue printed on 1835-07-01
what_it_does_not_supply: any building's form, material, storey count, fenestration or dimensions — an advertisement describes a trade, not a building
the specific corner of any junction it names: 'on the corner of' does not say which of the four
anything at all from an engraving — see trap 1; the cuts are the printer's stock
proof that a business named in 1833 or 1834 still stood on 1835-07-01; that is ruling 3's survival liberty, and it is a liberty
an argument from silence, unless corpus.json shows the issues either side of the silence are both in the deposit
a reading that outranks a scan read of the same passage — see ruling 2 and the C. & I. HARMON case
a citation without an issue page and column
